item.text:
The audit closed with a correction that materially shrinks finding 3, plus a verified integrity statement.

**Finding 3 narrowed — I tried the fix and it doesn't hold up.** Implementing the "leader re-sends the missing entries to any lagging promised follower" fix in the diagnostic core copy changed nothing: the probe still ended at `decided 1=1 [1], 2=1 [1], 3=0 []` after 5000 rounds, and it broke the sibling test. The reason matters: the probe's filter drops *every* `AcceptDecide`/`Decide` addressed to that node, so it models a persistently one-way link and the retry is dropped by the same filter — no leader-side change can help. A second, genuinely useful observation came out of the attempt: re-sending an `AcceptSync` is a **no-op**, because `handle_acceptsync` only acts in `Phase::Prepare` while a lagging follower sits in `Phase::Accept`. I reverted the attempt (the diagnostic core copy is instrumentation-only again) and recorded both facts in the report, where finding 3 is now presented as a *source-grounded observation* — the leader never rebuilds a lagging follower, the follower re-sends nothing in `Phase::Accept`, `Outdated` is dropped silently — rather than a proven defect, alongside the earlier trace finding that the re-sent StopSign `Decide` reuses an already-consumed sequence number and cannot take effect. The executive summary now leads with two confirmed defects (each with a deterministic repro *and* a validated fix) and this narrowed third item.

**Integrity of the captured source verified at handoff**: `omnipaxos/src`, `omnipaxos_runtime/src`, `omnipaxos_storage/src` and the manifests are byte-identical to the read-only `source/` tree by `diff -rq`; the only additions anywhere are the report, `repro.sh`, the four `audit_*` test files, the instrumented diagnostic copies under `diag/`, and the logs under `notes/`.
